Scale and detail

Start from a photograph taken as front-on as possible. Strong perspective distorts widths and heights and forces correction before conversion to a grid.

Work in stitch dimensions rather than pixels alone. The same artwork may work at 120 stitches wide and lose its identity completely when reduced to 45. Color and style

Remove cars, wires, bins and vegetation that hide the architecture unless they have sentimental value. An important garden can remain; an accidentally parked car usually does not need to.

Limit colors deliberately. Every extra shade should add volume, separation or identity; if it appears in only a few stitches without changing the image, it may add work rather than quality. Composition and personalization

Reduce facade materials into readable color masses. Stone, brick and wood can be suggested with a few shades and selective texture rather than photographic confetti.

Think about the final use as well: gift, framed art, mini, collection or personalization.
